raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've farmed this land in Quzhou for 40 years. I know the soil, I know the seasons. My wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of what I do — it's reliable, I can manage most of it with machines now, and the grain can be sold or kept for the household. With 9 mouths at home and some of the younger ones working off-farm, I can't depend on their labor for the whole season. That's partly why I keep wheat-maize as the main system — I can mostly handle it myself, especially with the neighbors sharing a rotary tiller.

Cotton gives me cash income, but it's hard work, especially at my age. I'll keep about 3 mu of cotton. I won't expand it — the price isn't as good as it used to be, and I can't spend all day bending over picking. Seven mu for wheat-maize rotation, 3.1 mu for cotton.

For wheat I'll buy improved seed — same variety I've used the past several years, Jimai series. It does well here. For maize I always use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has that's similar. Better yield. For cotton I use a Bt hybrid variety — fewer bollworm sprays needed, which saves me time.

Fertilizer: I apply base fertilizer at sowing and top-dress at key stages. My rates are probably a bit heavier than what the extension station recommends, but that's how I've always gotten good yields. I'm not going to change now. Irrigation from the well — wheat needs 3 waterings here in Hebei, that's just the reality of our dry springs. Cotton I'll water 3 times. Maize can usually get by on rainfall plus 2 waterings.

For tillage: rotary for wheat seedbed preparation, no-till for maize after wheat harvest (saves time and fuel), and I'll plough the cotton field properly before planting.
